outcome_or_open_work: Rat feeding and topical touch studies do not measure handwriting or hand motor performance.
No tested toasted oil rigidity endpoint. Whole nuts with exploratory movement and pooled rat behavior do not measure rigidity.

Previously dated gastrointestinal-lesion and surgical-adhesion models measured tissue pathology. Search included human carrier oil and multiple nociceptive assays without a verifiable rated pain result after exposure.
Hazelnut-fed imaging protocols measure working memory. Hallucination counts and medication-related events remain unresolved.
Assigned oral oil trial gives timed urine collection, pooled volume and contaminant excretion. Participants were instructed to void on the schedule. The study measured no urinary urgency.
Topical hazelnut oil studies measure cheek sensation, skin variables and touch. No facial-expression endpoint.
Prior whole nuts and rat oil feeding measure open-field locomotion or unspecified aggregate behavior without tremor rating.
Existing cold-pressed fly oil study measures geotaxis and cell report measures viability. No dystonic posture or clinical pattern assessment.
No oil-linked abnormal involuntary movement scale or levodopa dyskinesia contrast identified. Climbing and maze performance are distinct.
Walnut comparator had more bathroom-related sleep interruption than an essential-oil blend in cardiac rehabilitation. Bedside aroma and nocturnal interruption do not establish urinary urgency.

Whole walnut crossover used a validated adult sleepiness scale. The oil comparator cardiac paper did not separately report daytime dysfunction. Direct walnut oil grade and Parkinson effect remain open.
Walnut aroma comparator gives a null bad-dream item contrast and no PSG, REM muscle tone or dream enactment behavior. Continue specific parasomnia endpoints.
Whole walnut snack had no clear salivary-flow increase. The published walnut-oil food-engineering hydrogel did not test people. Neither measures drooling after oral cold-pressed walnut oil.

Whole walnut human balance study and animal latency-to-fall studies provide variable results. Cold-pressed walnut fly climbing does not measure fall frequency. Exact oil and clinical falls remain unresolved.
